ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: A certain wet material undergoes adiabatic drying in an atmospheric-pressure dryer; the amount of product after drying is 4000kg/h, the moisture content of the wet material is 15\% ($\alpha_\text{wet}$ basis, the same below), and the moisture content of the product must not be higher than 1\%. The initial temperature of the air is 20°C, and the relative humidity is 40\%. The air is preheated to 120°C and then enters the dryer, and the temperature of the gas leaving the dryer is selected as 70°C. The change process of the air and material in the drying system is as shown in the figure. Find the thermal efficiency of the dryer.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows: The air state on the left is t0=20°C, relative humidity φ0=40%; the air first enters the “preheating” device, and heat supply Qp is marked above the preheater; after preheating, the air enters the “drying” device at t1=120°C; after the air passes through the adiabatic dryer, it is discharged from the right side, and the outlet temperature is labeled t2=70°C. The figure also shows wet material entering the dryer and product flowing out, but calculating the thermal efficiency according to the specified method only needs the three temperatures of the air. Reasoning: The dryer thermal efficiency is calculated according to η=(t1−t2)/(t1−t0)×100%. Substituting t0=20°C, t1=120°C, t2=70°C gives η=(120−70)/(120−20)×100%=50/100×100%=50%.

raw_record.question_text: A certain wet material undergoes adiabatic drying in an atmospheric-pressure dryer; the amount of product after drying is 4000kg/h, the moisture content of the wet material is 15\% ($\alpha_\text{wet}$ basis, the same below), and the moisture content of the product must not be higher than 1\%. The initial temperature of the air is 20°C, and the relative humidity is 40\%. The air is preheated to 120°C and then enters the dryer, and the temperature of the gas leaving the dryer is selected as 70°C. The change process of the air and material in the drying system is as shown in the figure. Find the thermal efficiency of the dryer.

method.method_draft: First describe the image process: air is preheated from 20°C to 120°C, then cools through the adiabatic dryer to 70°C. From the text/image take t0=20°C, t1=120°C, and t2=70°C. Apply η=(t1−t2)/(t1−t0)×100%. Compute η=(120−70)/(120−20)×100%=50%. Report the dryer heat efficiency as 50%.
method.CoT_raw: 图像显示：左侧空气状态为 t0=20°C、相对湿度 φ0=40%，空气先进入“预热”器，预热器上方标有供热 Qp；预热后空气以 t1=120°C 进入“干燥”器；空气经过绝热干燥器后从右侧排出，出口温度标为 t2=70°C。图中还显示湿物料进入干燥器、产品流出，但按指定方法计算热效率只需使用空气的三个温度。推理：干燥器热效率按 η=(t1−t2)/(t1−t0)×100% 计算。代入 t0=20°C、t1=120°C、t2=70°C，得 η=(120−70)/(120−20)×100%=50/100×100%=50%。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct thermodynamic-efficiency route based on the process temperatures shown in the diagram; it does not require a full material balance because the standard dryer heat-efficiency definition here is the fraction of preheated-air sensible heat actually dropped inside the dryer.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the flow sequence from the diagram: ambient air at t0=20°C, φ0=40% enters a preheater; after heat input Qp it leaves the preheater at t1=120°C with humidity H1; it then enters an adiabatic dryer and exits as waste gas at t2=70°C with humidity H2. The diagram also shows wet feed G1, w1=15%, and product G2=4000 kg/h, w2≤1%, but these are not needed for this efficiency definition.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the text to confirm the operating assumptions: atmospheric adiabatic drying, air initially at 20°C and 40% RH, preheated to 120°C before the dryer, exhaust gas selected at 70°C, and requested quantity is dryer heat efficiency.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the drying-theory definition for an adiabatic dryer heated only by preheated air: thermal efficiency equals useful sensible heat released by the hot air in the dryer divided by the heat supplied in preheating the air. With nearly the same humid-air heat capacity over both intervals, this reduces to η=(t1−t2)/(t1−t0)×100%.
